recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Any future change for the special :not behavior with comma-separated values should follow the later FHIR-40629 follow-up path rather than changing FHIR-13307's general modifier/OR rule.
issue_request: FHIR-13307 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for STU3 asking the Search page to clarify whether comma-separated OR values are allowed when a search parameter uses a modifier; the Jira specifically noted :missing as an exception and :in as an example that should allow multiple values.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 8200d5f1f3ca93e5ebb38d464a3691320d312572, matching Jira comment svn revision 12862, by adding text to source/search.html that every search parameter may use comma-separated values including modifiers such as ?code:text=this,that.
additional_context: Later final Search-page changes reorganized and clarified the wording. FHIR-33158 moved the AND/OR material out of the Composite Search Parameters section into a dedicated multiple-values section, and FHIR-40629 added explicit modifier OR examples plus a separate dragon note for the :not edge case. The original Zulip thread for :in modifier confirms the ambiguity that led Lloyd to create GF#13307, while the later :not thread led to FHIR-40629 rather than reversing the general rule.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. Current source/search.html defines comma-separated OR values, gives a modifier example with given:exact=GivenA,GivenB, and repeats in the Modifiers section that modifiers are allowed with multiple terms and apply to all OR-joined values.

related_jiras.note: Reorganized the Search page combining/composite wording and preserved the comma-separated OR rule in a dedicated multiple-values section.
Clarified that modifiers apply to all OR-joined values and recorded a separate unresolved :not edge-case discussion.
